title: continuous-batcher: scheduler tuning for queueing fairness, starvation prevention, and timeouts
author: Ava Chen
description:
Motivation: Several customers and canaries reported intermittent tail latency spikes and request starvation under high-concurrency workloads. The continuous-batcher scheduler previously prioritized throughput which allowed long-lived queues for low-priority routes and large-context requests to starve short, latency-sensitive requests. This PR tunes the continuous batching scheduler to improve queueing fairness, add starvation prevention, and introduce configurable request-level timeouts.

Summary of changes: 1) Introduce fairness_score per request that combines age, priority, and estimated token cost. 2) Add aging-based promotion: requests that exceed a configurable max_queue_time_ms are bumped in scheduling weight. 3) Implement per-route soft_timeouts and hard_timeouts: soft timeout triggers best-effort flush, hard timeout cancels the request and returns a partial response; both are configurable via runtime flags and route config. 4) Integrate KV-cache awareness into scheduling decisions: requests likely to hit KV cache are favored to improve throughput without increasing latency for cache misses. 5) Add new metrics (scheduler.queue_age_p999, scheduler.fairness_rebalances, scheduler.timeout_evictions) and dashboards. 6) Add unit and integration tests for priority ordering, aging promotion, and timeout behavior.

Rollout plan: feature gated behind runtime flag continuous_batcher.fairness_enabled (default: off). Will enable in staging for 48h, run perf canaries, then ramp to 20% on production with telemetry alerts for queue_age_p99/p999 regressions.

review_comments: Diego Martinez (2026-02-21): Can you explain why we combine age and estimated token cost rather than normalizing to expected service time? Request: add a short comment in score_calculator explaining the heuristic.
Ava Chen (2026-02-21): Reply: We normalize by estimated tokens in the fairness_score computation; added a comment and a unit test to demonstrate ordering under mixed token distributions.
Priya Nair (2026-02-22): Nit: prefer soft/hard timeout names in config to be explicit (soft_timeout_ms / hard_timeout_ms). Also please add metric for soft timeout occurrences.
Ava Chen (2026-02-22): Done — renamed config fields and added scheduler.timeout_soft_evictions metric.
Samir Patel (2026-02-24): Observability: add a p50/p95/p999 histogram for queue_age per priority class. Also make sure the aging promotion doesn't thrash small batches under high load.
Ava Chen (2026-02-25): Added histograms and tuned promotion window to 20ms minimum hold to avoid thrashing. Benchmarks attached.
CI (2026-02-26): Integration test flaky on macOS runner - reran, all green.
Diego Martinez (2026-02-27): Approved — verified canary dashboards show reduced p999 tail for low-priority routes and no regression on high-priority service times.
Release Manager (2026-02-28): Merged via squash to main.
performance_summary: Staging perf-canary results: average throughput unchanged, overall token/sec +3%. Tail latency improvements: p99 reduced by ~12% for mixed workloads, p999 reduced by ~20% on low-priority-heavy scenarios. Starvation cases (previously observed at 95th percentile queue age > 800ms) reduced to < 50ms after aging-based promotion. Timeout evictions accounted for <0.05% of requests with default conservative settings.
release_notes: Improved continuous-batcher scheduler: fairness-aware scheduling, aging-based promotion to prevent starvation, configurable soft/hard timeouts, and KV-cache-aware scheduling that improves tail latency under mixed workloads. Feature is feature-gated and disabled by default; enable via continuous_batcher.fairness_enabled. (ENG-2145)
